item.title: Even With High Approval Ratings, Is Takaichi’s Snap Election a Political Gamble?
item.description: Takaichi could seek to capitalize on her popularity by dissolving the lower house and calling an early election. However, support for the LDP has stayed persistently low.

item.title: China’s Muted Response to Venezuela: Sober Alarm, Not Nationalist Bombast
item.description: The official Chinese narrative foregrounds international condemnation and positions Beijing as defender of the international order. But Chinese commentary strikes a different tone.

item.title: The New Age of Maritime Multilateralism in the Indian Ocean
item.description: The South Asian littorals are shaping a polycentric security order.

item.title: Privilege Over Rights: Appropriating Indigenous Peoples’ Entitlements in Malaysia
item.description: The belated move to update a 71-year-old law exposes Malaysia’s long-standing failure to safeguard the rights of the Orang Asli.

item.title: China’s Multilayered Approach to Rare Earths Under US-Led Decoupling
item.description: Amid intense focus on export restrictions and decoupling, far less attention has been paid to how China is responding to U.S.-led diversification efforts.

item.title: Indian Perception of Russian Power Is Outdated
item.description: In the contemporary world, Russia neither has the will nor the ability to unfailingly support India.

item.title: Why South Korea’s Welfare State Fails Its Elderly
item.description: Low pension adequacy, restrictive safety nets, and life-course inequality explain why old age so often means poverty in Korea.

item.title: The US Cannot Push China out of Latin America
item.description: China’s role in Latin America is built on trade flows, long-term investment, financial links, and large-scale infrastructure projects that benefit both sides.

item.title: China Won’t Save Iran’s Regime – But Chinese Surveillance Technology Might
item.description: Yes, China’s response to the violence in Iran has been muted. But don’t overlook the support that China has already provided in the form of surveillance and drone technology.

item.title: How Western Companies Helped Create Their Chinese Competitors – Like Labubu
item.description: Labubu’s success draws on capabilities derived from Western branding and advertising practices over the past two decades – combined with China’s extremely low-cost labor model.
